title: DNS & DHCP for Windows Server Interviews

scenes.line1: Why does AD break so often?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why Active Directory issues pop up so much? Is it really the domain that's broken?

scenes.label: DNS
scenes.sub: Domain controllers register service records so clients can find them.
scenes.say: Here's the deal: domain controllers use DNS to register special service records. That's how clients actually find them.

scenes.label: DHCP
scenes.sub: DHCP hands out IP addresses from defined scopes.
scenes.say: And DHCP? It hands out IP addresses from scopes you set up, so every device gets a unique address.

scenes.title: Check DNS records
scenes.say: If something's off, use the lookup command to check if your app or domain controller records show up. If the service record is missing, DNS is the real culprit.

scenes.question: SRV lookup is empty. What next?
scenes.right: Fix DNS first—AD relies on DNS to work.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: if your service record lookup comes back empty, don't jump to fixing Active Directory. Always fix DNS first.
